- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match true mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and overpredicts continuation; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.5 over 3–5 days), model frequently underestimates upside; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–7 days to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion after prolonged sideways or downward trends; if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish, forecast should be slightly below recent 10-day average to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +0.25/-0.5), model often fails to smooth transitions; use weighted average of recent 7-day trend + sentiment signal to dampen erratic swings.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility in early days; cap forecast variance within ±20% of 14-day moving average to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
